source.title: Excess Risk of Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks in Teacher-Student Settings and its Superiority to Kernel Methods

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: Studies two-phase gradient training in a new setting—two-layer ReLU teacher-student regression—and reports theoretical and experimental outcomes. It does not test the listed classification, local-minimum frequency, initialization comparison, learning-rate, depth, or normalization versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's numerical experiment reports training and test loss for its own two-phase algorithm. Cited results from other studies are excluded. The figure does not provide readable numeric values in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes its own two-phase optimization algorithm and regression excess risk. It does not test any listed version. Its discussion of spurious minima under ordinary gradient descent cites prior work; its own noisy-gradient method does not measure V2's width-dependent frequency of convergence to spurious minima.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish a near-parametric excess-risk upper bound for a same-width two-layer ReLU student trained by their two-phase algorithm. Comparing it with a minimax lower bound for linear estimators, they conclude a statistical-rate advantage over kernel methods under their assumptions, attributed to adaptive feature learning in the non-convex model.
record.recipe_differences: Two-phase method: noisy gradient descent with weight decay, clipping, and Gaussian noise, followed by vanilla gradient descent. The task is teacher-student regression with squared loss, rather than the classification settings in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper uses different optimization procedures in phase I and phase II; its Figure 1 describes a loss-trajectory change at the phase transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4.6 bounds same-width student regression excess risk by a constant times log n/n under its assumptions and specified two-phase algorithm. Figure 1 qualitatively illustrates convergence for d=m=10 and n=1000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the specified teacher-student regression setting, noisy gradient descent followed by local vanilla gradient descent can learn a same-width two-layer ReLU teacher with a near-parametric excess-risk rate.

record.problems: The experiment is one setting (d = m = 10, n = 1000); Figure 1 is the only supplied evidence for its loss trajectory and the text gives no numeric training-loss values. The theorem concerns regression excess risk, not classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results identified. Statements about the results of cited prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and recipe or size comparisons.

Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization or normalization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, orthogonality, and trainable depth.

record.verdict_notes: Same-width convergence under an algorithm with added gradient noise does not challenge V2's finding about ordinary gradient descent. The experiment's positive training-loss floor under noisy regression targets does not challenge V1's classification-error claim.

Depth comparisons, identity shortcuts, plain networks, and normalization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness changes, recovery, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.
